doc.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023

title: Memorable SNL shows: Joe Cocker and Bryan Ferry
summary: He recalls Stuff backing Joe Cocker with Belushi, then the Bryan Ferry show where he covered Sammy Figueroa's conga part and pulled Steve Jordan on stage.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Anybody stand out — a particular show that comes to mind when someone like me asks about Saturday Night Live?

Well the shows that we did with Stuff, you know backing up Joe Cocker. Somebody just posted them on FaceBook recently. You know we did “Feelin’ All Right” with Joe Cocker and John Belushi comes out and surprises him, imitating Joe Cocker, which broke Joe Cocker’s heart. I mean it was a total surprise to him. And then we do another tune, “Foots” in the second half of the show, which is really the band at its finest. You know everybody’s playing great and everybody’s alive. There’s another show with Bryan Ferry doing I think the tune was called “The Right Stuff” which was the name of his album. And I was playing percussion, just a shaker and tambourine. Sammy Figueroa was the percussionist and Andy Newmark, great drummer, was playing with Bryan Ferry. And we rehearsed, everything was cool. And I had a relatively, you know, laid back part, shaker and tambourine, cowbell or something. So I was enjoying it, it was great. And the dress rehearsal went fine, the rehearsals went fine. Between the dress rehearsal and the actual air show Sammy Figueroa went outside, you know went to get a breath of fresh air

and he couldn’t get back into the building. I don’t know if he forgot his ID or somebody wouldn’t let him back into the building. So it’s 11:59 or something and the band is about to go on and Bryan Ferry said, “I need that conga part, I need the percussion part.” And Sammy had a set-up of five drums, five congas. And I’d been digging him all week. So he said, “Can you play the conga part?” And I said uhhh sure. So I played this conga part and literally ten seconds before air I spotted Steve Jordan in the audience standing on the floor. And I said, “Steve, come on up and play.” I gave him the part that I was playing, a big shaker and a cowbell and a tambourine. I said, play, we’re going to do this. Air. Red light went on. So I’m playing this conga part that was killing my hands. My hands were like two pork chops after that. And Steve is playing shaker and tambourine. And we’re looking at each other during the thing. And Andy Newmark is like, “What the fu—“ — but it came off. So that was a very exciting show to say the least.
